previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease status post bypass, and diabetes was admitted after experiencing chest pain and bradycardia in the morning. He was found to have severe hyperkalemia (K 7.6), which was treated with intravenous calcium, insulin, and urgent hemodialysis. His chest pain and junctional rhythm resolved with potassium correction. Evaluation showed no evidence of acute myocardial infarction, with stable cardiac enzymes and a preserved ejection fraction on echocardiogram, though mild regional wall motion abnormality was noted. He had signs of mild volume overload on chest X-ray, consistent with acute on chronic diastolic heart failure. His lisinopril and metoprolol were held initially and restarted at discharge, with lisinopril dose increased to 5 mg daily. Sevelamer was doubled to help control potassium. He was discharged home after two days in stable condition with instructions to adhere to a low-potassium diet and attend all dialysis sessions.
